speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your consultation. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To begin my assessment, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any changes in your urinary or bowel habits?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Tumor_Markers_CEA_Ca125_Ca199

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin: 12.8 g/dL, Platelets: 275,000 /μL, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS, Tumor_Markers_CEA_Ca125_Ca199: CEA: NORMAL READINGS, Ca125: Normal, Ca199: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Since the previous doctor suggested pyelonephritis, which contradicts your large ovarian mass, I need to clarify the symptoms of your mass itself. Have you noticed any pelvic pressure, pain, or changes in your menstrual cycle?

REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound, CT_Abdomen_Pelvis
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_images

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present; CT_Abdomen_Pelvis: Not available; Ultrasound_images: Not available

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Carcinoma. The combination of a large ovarian mass, significant ascites, and shortness of breath is highly characteristic of advanced ovarian cancer; the previous suggestion of pyelonephritis is inconsistent with these specific findings.
